sources.citation: Zogbo, Lynell Marchese. 2019. Central vowels in the Kru language family: innovation and areal spreading. In Clem, Jenks & Sande (eds), Theory and description in African Linguistics (ACAL 47), 725-750. Berlin: Language Science Press.
sources.note: Only Kodia content is one lexical form (n4 gbɤ3 'five', 'Kodia (Leidenfrost, p.c.)') and map placement; nothing on Kodia stress or tone system.

sources.note: 'Kwadia' appears only as a node label in the Eastern Kru tree; no data.

sources.citation: Vogler, Pierre. 2017/2024. Contribution à la classification des langues kru (Niger-Congo). Ms., Université de Strasbourg (HAL hal-01574391 / hal-04390526).
sources.note: Searched (diacritic-stripped) for kodia/kwadia/kwadya/kodya: no mention at all; Kodia is not in Vogler's comparative data.

sources.citation: Gibbon, Dafydd. 2016. Legacy language atlas data mining: mapping Kru languages. Proceedings of LREC 2016, 3235-3242. ELRA.
sources.note: Nothing on stress. Useful negative evidence: lists the 19 Kru languages for which Marchese's 1984 Atlas linguistique kru gives consonant systems (Aizi, Bassa, Bete, Cedepo, Dewoin, Dida de Lozoua, Dida F, Godie, Grebo, Guere, Klao, Koyo, Krahn, Kuwaa, Neyo, Niaboua, Seme, Tepo, Wobe) -- Kodia/Kwadia is not among them, so even the Atlas apparently has no phonological sketch of Kodia.

sources.citation: Eberhard, Simons & Fennig (eds). Ethnologue: Kodia [kwp] (17th ed. 2013, 19th ed. 2016, 22nd ed. 2019; archived copies).
sources.note: 840 speakers (1993 SIL), Bas-Sassandra, 6b Threatened, unwritten, classification Kru > Eastern > Kwadia; no typology field, nothing on stress or tone.

sources.citation: Delafosse, Maurice. 1904. Vocabulaires comparatifs de plus de 60 langues ou dialectes parlés à la Côte d'Ivoire et dans les régions limitrophes. Paris: Leroux.
sources.note: Locates the 'Kwadya ou Kwadre' on both banks of the Sassandra (said to be a Bete-Bakwe mixture) but states explicitly 'sauf en Kwadya, en Pia et en Gim, n'ayant encore pu recueillir aucun document sur ces trois dialectes' -- no Kwadya data at all; only a general remark that 'l'accent tonique ou plutôt l'intonation' cannot be marked alphabetically.
